notionImport.title: Import into Docs
notionImport.lead: Bring pages from Notion, Confluence, Google Docs, Word or Evernote with their tree, images, files and links between pages.
notionImport.step1: In Notion, open Settings › Export all workspace content, or ··· › Export on a single page.
notionImport.step2: Choose Markdown & CSV, include subpages, and include files and images.
notionImport.step3: Upload the .zip that Notion gives you here.
notionImport.fileHelp: Up to 1 GB. The file is deleted when the import ends.
notionImport.already: {count} pages were imported before and will be skipped.
notionImport.doneSummary: {pages} pages and {databases} databases imported with {files} files. {skipped} skipped.
notionImport.filesSkipped: {count} files were not uploaded (over 10 MB or a type we do not store) and stay as their name.
notionImport.rowsNote: The page of each database row goes in as the body of that row, not as a separate page.
notionImport.doneRows: {count, plural, one {# database row kept its page as the body} other {# database rows kept their pages as the body}}.

notion.name: Notion
notion.step1: In Notion, open Settings › Export all workspace content, or ··· › Export on a single page.
notion.step2: Choose Markdown & CSV (or HTML), include subpages, and include files and images.
notion.step3: Upload the .zip that Notion gives you here.

confluence.name: Confluence
confluence.step1: In Confluence, open the space and go to Space settings › Export space.
confluence.step2: Choose HTML, export all pages (or the ones you want) and download the .zip.
confluence.step3: Upload it here: the space becomes a page with its tree, images and attachments.

gdocs.name: Google Docs
gdocs.step1: One document: File › Download › Microsoft Word (.docx) or Web page (.html, zipped).
gdocs.step2: A whole folder: download it from Google Drive (or use Google Takeout) and keep the .zip.
gdocs.step3: Upload the file here: folders become pages with their documents inside.

word.name: Word (.docx)
word.step1: Save the document as .docx (Word, Pages or LibreOffice can do it).
word.step2: For several documents, put them in a .zip, with folders if you want a tree.
word.step3: Upload it here: headings, lists, tables, links and images come in.

evernote.name: Evernote
evernote.step1: In Evernote, right-click a notebook and choose Export notebook.
evernote.step2: Choose ENEX (.enex). For several notebooks, put the .enex files in a .zip.
evernote.step3: Upload it here: each notebook becomes a page with one subpage per note, with its images, to-dos and tags.

files.name: Markdown, HTML or other files
files.step1: Any .md, .txt, .html or .docx file, or a .zip with many of them.
files.step2: In a .zip, each folder becomes a page and links between files become links between pages.
files.step3: Images next to the files come in as image blocks.
